paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: bridges the official COROS (高驰) MCP server with a self-contained stdio<->HT
TP bridge and on-device OAuth login. 34 COROS tools for sleep/HRV/RHR/recovery/training-load, activi
ties and FIT files, plus workout and training-plan APIs.
# dsh-coros-mcp
Bridges the official **COROS (高驰) MCP** server into DeepSeek Harness. One install exposes the full `
mcp__coros__*` tool set: sleep, HRV, resting heart rate, recovery, training load, activities and FIT
files, plus workout / training-plan CRUD and scheduling (34 tools on the current endpoint; may chan
ge with the server).
Self-contained: the stdio bridge, the OAuth login flow and token refresh all live in this package. N
o external CLI, no absolute paths in your profile, no local callback port.
## Highlights
- **Zero runtime dependencies** — plain Node.js built-ins (`fetch`, `crypto`, `fs`, `http`); nothing

to `npm install`.
- **Self-contained OAuth** — dynamic client registration + PKCE(S256) + COROS CLI
login-session flow; `login-start` / `login-finish` are separate processes and open **no local port*

*.
- **Survives DSH upgrades** — `engines.dsh` is a bottomless minimum (`>=0.2.1-rc.1`), and if a fu
ture DSH changes the MCP-client JS API the plugin falls back to mounting the same row through the co

re Cordis Loader. It is not silently gated off by a version bump.
- **Tokens stay local** — `~/.dsh/
coros-mcp/<region>/token.json` (0600), outside the profile config, never printed in logs, no telemet

ry, no third-party server in the data path.
- **Bridge fixes real MCP schema issues** — COROS serves
`tools/list` schemas with top-level `$defs`/`$ref`; the bridge inlines them so providers do not rej

ect `createScheduledWorkout` with `Pointer '/$defs/Section' does not exist`.
- **Rotation-safe refre
sh** — COROS rotates the refresh token on every refresh; bridge and login CLI serialise refreshes wi

th one cross-process file lock.
- **Works Outside DSH too** — `lib/proxy.mjs` is a standard MCP stdi
o server usable from any MCP client.
## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The bridge exists because DSH's MCP client speaks stdio / static headers while the COROS endpoint re
quires expiring OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens.
Login (`lib/login.mjs`) uses COROS' gateway CLI login session: dynamic client registration + PKCE(S2
56) + browser authorization + polling for the one-time `loginTicket` + server-side code exchange. No
local listener is started, so `login-start` and `login-finish` are independent processes and Window
s has no port conflicts.
## Does a DSH upgrade disable it?
**No longer because of a version mismatch.** How it works:
- At profile start DSH evaluates `engines.dsh` (`app-boot` → `evaluatePluginCompatibility`) with `se
mver.satisfies(..., { includePrerelease: true })`. Earlier builds declared a **finite** range (the 0
.2.1 line plus a single 0.2.2 RC); when DSH auto-updated to a newer RC the range no longer matched,

so the plugin was skipped silently — that is why the COROS tools disappeared after a DSH update.
- S
ince 1.0.2 `engines.dsh` is a **bottomless minimum**: `>=0.2.1-rc.1`. With `includePrerelease: true`
that covers 0.2.1, 0.2.2, future 0.2.x RCs, 0.3.x, 1.x — **normal DSH upgrades will not gate it out

again**.
- Belt and braces: if a future DSH release changes the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` JS ex
ports, the plugin falls back to mounting the same MCP-client row through the core Cordis Loader (`ct
x.loader.create`, the same path profile patches use). Only when both registration paths fail does it

log an explicit `[coros-mcp] could not attach the DSH MCP client` warning.
- The one case not guara
nteed: a breaking DSH API change where both registration paths are gone. Install a freshly built plu
gin for that DSH version; tokens and login state are unaffected.
> A GitHub/tarball install does not auto-upgrade the plugin itself; re-run `dsh plugin add <new tgz>
` when a new build is available.
## Install
Requires DeepSeek Harness ≥ `0.2.1-rc.1` (`engines.dsh` is a bottomless range, so future versions ar
e not blocked) and Node.js ≥ 20 (the DSH runtime provides one).
[代码示例省略，未执行]

> No local build needed: download `dsh-coros-mcp-<version>.tgz` from GitHub Releases,
> or install s
traight from the repository: `dsh plugin --profile desktop add 'github:xsnnnnnn/dsh-coros'`.
Then enable `dsh-coros-mcp` in **Settings → Plugins** and restart DSH if needed.
> Migrating from a hand-wired setup: back up the profile `cordis.patch.yml` and delete the manual `i
d: mcp-coros` `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` row. Keeping both registers the same `mcp__coros__*` too
l names twice and the tool registration fails.
## Login
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- Tokens live in `~/.dsh/coros-mcp/<region>/token.json` (0600, atomic writes). That is outside the p

rofile directory, so profile-config backups never capture them.
- Existing `~/.coros-mcp-skill-gatew
ay-ts/<region>/token.json` (the official COROS CLI cache) is read as a fallback, so an existing logi
n keeps working with zero migration. A new login writes to the plugin-owned path, which wins afterwa

rds.
- Access tokens last 30 days. The **refresh token rotates on every refresh and the old value di
es immediately**, so the bridge and the login CLI serialise refreshes with one file lock (`token.jso

n.lock`).
- Region: inferred from the cache; override with `--region cn|eu|us` or configuration.
## Privacy
Tokens never leave the machine, are stored 0600 outside the profile, and are never printed; logs con
tain only region, endpoint and expiry metadata. The plugin makes no network request at startup — onl
y tool calls, `--selftest` and explicit login/refresh commands reach COROS.
## Compatibility & license
- `engines.dsh`: `>=0.2.1-rc.1` (**no upper bound**, covers future releases; DSH evaluates with `inc

ludePrerelease: true`); `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases`: `0.2.1-rc.5`, `0.2.2-rc.1` = compatible.
-

Node.js ≥ 20, no third-party runtime dependencies.
- MIT. COROS and 高驰 are trademarks of their owner

; this project is unofficial.
- Protocol details were derived from the public COROS gateway endpoint
s and the official CLI's observable behaviour; no code from the UNLICENSED official npm packages is
CLI's observable behaviour; no code from the UNLICENSED official npm packages is copied or bundled.
See README.zh.md for the full Chinese documentation.
